q1: SELECT ITM.ITEMN, ITPV.VENDN FROM ITM AS ITM, (SELECT DISTINCT ITP.ITEMN, PUR.VENDN FROM ITP AS ITP, PUR AS PUR WHERE ITP.PONUM = PUR.PONUM AND PUR.ODATE > 85) AS ITPV WHERE ITM.ITEMN = ITPV.ITEMN AND ITM.ITEMN > 1 AND ITM.ITEMN < 20
q2: SELECT DISTINCT ITM.ITEMN, PUR.VENDN FROM ITM AS ITM, ITP AS ITP, PUR AS PUR WHERE ITP.PONUM = PUR.PONUM AND ITM.ITEMN = ITP.ITEMN AND PUR.ODATE > 85 AND ITM.ITEMN > 1 AND ITM.ITEMN < 20
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT ITM.ITEMN, ITPV.VENDN FROM ITM AS ITM, (SELECT DISTINCT ITP.ITEMN, PUR.VENDN FROM ITP AS ITP, PUR AS PUR WHERE ITP.PONUM = PUR.PONUM AND PUR.ODATE > 85) AS ITPV WHERE ITM.ITEMN = ITPV.ITEMN AND ITM.ITEMN > 1 AND ITM.ITEMN < 20
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT ITM.ITEMN, PUR.VENDN FROM ITM AS ITM, ITP AS ITP, PUR AS PUR WHERE ITP.PONUM = PUR.PONUM AND ITM.ITEMN = ITP.ITEMN AND PUR.ODATE > 85 AND ITM.ITEMN > 1 AND ITM.ITEMN < 20
counterexample: INSERT INTO ITM (ITEMN) VALUES (2); INSERT INTO ITM (ITEMN) VALUES (3); INSERT INTO ITP (ITEMN, PONUM) VALUES (2, 100); INSERT INTO ITP (ITEMN, PONUM) VALUES (2, 200); INSERT INTO PUR (PONUM, ODATE, VENDN) VALUES (100, 86, 1); INSERT INTO PUR (PONUM, ODATE, VENDN) VALUES (200, 86, 2);
explanation: Q1 uses a subquery with DISTINCT on ITP and PUR, then joins with ITM. Q2 performs a three-way join without a subquery but also uses DISTINCT. The difference lies in the ordering of operations and potential for different result sets due to the DISTINCT placement, leading to possible inequivalence.
counterexample_dsp: A scenario where ITP has duplicate ITEMN entries across different PONUMs, and PUR has multiple PONUMs with the same ODATE > 85. Q1 will return distinct ITEMN and VENDN combinations from the subquery, while Q2 may produce more duplicates before applying DISTINCT.
